title: Hello at the door
aim: Greet someone and say your name.

lines.en: My name is Anna. This is my friend.

title: Who is this?
aim: Point to a person and say who they are.

lines.en: The child is here with me.

title: Good morning
aim: Use a greeting that fits the time of day.

title: Please and thank you
aim: Ask for something and thank the person.

title: Yes and no
aim: Accept or refuse a simple offer.

title: My family
aim: Name the people in your family.

lines.en: Yes. And this is my father.

title: In the house
aim: Name the rooms and the door.

lines.en: The key is on the table.

title: At the table
aim: Say where something is.

lines.en: The water is on the table too.

title: Breakfast
aim: Say what you eat in the morning.

lines.en: I eat bread and an egg.

title: I am hungry
aim: Say you want food or drink.

title: Numbers one to five
aim: Count a few things you can see.

lines.en: Yes. One is for the child.

title: How much?
aim: Ask the price of one thing.

title: The weather today
aim: Say if it is hot, cold, or raining.

lines.en: No. It is a good day.

title: What I see
aim: Name what you see outside.

title: Left and right
aim: Follow two simple directions.

title: What time is it?
aim: Ask and say a simple time.

title: My day
aim: Name three parts of the day.

lines.en: In the evening I am at home.

title: Getting dressed
aim: Name a few clothes.

lines.en: Your shoes are by the door.

title: Colours
aim: Describe a thing by colour.

lines.en: The blue one is here too.

title: Big and small
aim: Compare two sizes simply.

title: The body
aim: Name parts of the body you can point to.

lines.en: Your foot is wet from the rain.

title: I feel ill
aim: Say that something hurts, simply.

title: At school
aim: Say you are a student and name the classroom.

title: Open your book
aim: Follow a classroom instruction.

title: I do not understand
aim: Ask someone to repeat.

title: On the bus
aim: Ask for a stop in town.

title: The train
aim: Ask where the train is.

title: A phone call
aim: Answer and say who you are.

lines.en: Good. Or I can call later.

title: The neighbour
aim: Introduce yourself next door.

title: Come in
aim: Invite someone in and offer a seat.

title: The kitchen
aim: Name things you use to eat.

lines.en: The cups are by the water.

title: Fruit at the market
aim: Buy fruit and say the quantity.

title: I like it
aim: Say what you like and do not like.

title: The menu
aim: Order from two choices.

title: Paying
aim: Say you want to pay.

title: The bathroom
aim: Ask where the bathroom is.

title: Days of the week
aim: Name today and tomorrow.

title: The calendar
aim: Say a date simply.

title: At night
aim: Say that someone is sleeping.

title: The pet
aim: Talk about an animal at home.

lines.en: No. It is the neighbour's dog.

title: Work or study
aim: Say what you do.

lines.en: I have a job in town.

title: Where are you from?
aim: Ask and answer about home country.

lines.en: I am from a small city.
Yes. I live near the school.

title: The address
aim: Ask someone to write an address.

title: Lost
aim: Say you are lost and ask for the station.

title: The shop is closed
aim: Ask when a place opens.

title: A photo
aim: Ask before you take a picture.

title: The child is tired
aim: Talk about a child's needs.

title: Hot and cold drinks
aim: Choose a hot or cold drink.

title: See you soon
aim: End a conversation politely.

title: A short note
aim: Leave a simple message.

title: A train ticket
aim: Buy a ticket and ask the time.

lines.en: A return ticket to the city, please.

title: The train is late
aim: Ask why a train is delayed.

lines.en: Yes. There is a short delay.
About twenty minutes. Listen for the announcement.

title: Asking the way
aim: Follow a direction with two steps.

lines.en: How do I get to the market?
Go straight, then turn right at the corner.
No. I can show you on the map.

title: At the hotel desk
aim: Check in and ask for the room.

lines.en: I have a reservation. The name is Anna.
Yes. Here is your key. Room twelve.

title: A problem in the room
aim: Report something that does not work.

lines.en: I am sorry. I will send someone.

title: At the market
aim: Ask for a different piece of fruit.

lines.en: Yes. These are from this morning.

title: The wrong size
aim: Ask to try a smaller size.

lines.en: Would you like a smaller one?
Of course. The changing room is there.

title: Paying by card
aim: Ask if you can pay by card.

title: Returning something
aim: Explain that you want to return an item.

lines.en: Yes. I would like to return it.
We can exchange it or refund you.

title: Opening hours
aim: Ask when a place opens and closes.

lines.en: At nine, and we close at six.
No. We close for lunch from one to two.

title: At the pharmacy
aim: Ask for something for a headache.

title: A doctor's appointment
aim: Make an appointment for today or tomorrow.

title: Describing pain
aim: Say where it hurts and since when.

lines.en: Since last night. I have a fever too.

title: Calling in sick
aim: Tell work you cannot come because you are ill.

lines.en: I cannot come to the office today.
Yes. I need to stay home.

title: In class
aim: Ask the teacher to explain a word.

lines.en: Yes, and I will give an example.

title: Homework
aim: Ask when the homework is due.

lines.en: The homework is due on Friday.

title: The library
aim: Borrow a book and ask the return date.

lines.en: Do you have a library card?
Yes. When do I return it?

title: A group project
aim: Agree who does which part.

lines.en: Our project is about the city.

title: On the phone
aim: Leave a message for someone who is out.

lines.en: He is out. Can I take a message?
Please ask him to call me back.

title: A text message
aim: Say you will send the address.

lines.en: I will send you a text.
Yes. I do not have it now.
Send it later. That is fine.

title: At a restaurant
aim: Book a table and mention an allergy.

lines.en: A table for two at seven, please.
Inside. I have a nut allergy.

title: The bill
aim: Ask for the bill and check it.

title: This is not what I ordered
aim: Politely say the order is wrong.

lines.en: Excuse me. This is not what I ordered.
I am sorry. What did you ask for?

title: Cooking at home
aim: Say what you need for a simple meal.

title: The neighbour's noise
aim: Ask a neighbour to be quieter, politely.

lines.en: The music is loud in the evening.
I am sorry. I will keep it quiet.

title: Borrowing a tool
aim: Borrow something and say when you will return it.

title: The washing machine
aim: Explain that a machine is broken.

lines.en: I will call a repair person.

title: Plans for Saturday
aim: Invite someone and suggest a time.

lines.en: Shall we go to the cinema?

title: Yesterday
aim: Say what you did yesterday.

title: A hobby
aim: Talk about what you do in your free time.

lines.en: What do you do in your free time?

title: The weather forecast
aim: Talk about tomorrow's weather and clothes.

title: At the post office
aim: Send a parcel and ask the price.

lines.en: I want to send this parcel.
Four. It will arrive on Friday.

title: Lost property
aim: Describe something you lost.

lines.en: Someone found a black bag. Come and see.

title: A taxi
aim: Tell the driver where to go.

title: Renting a bike
aim: Rent something for one day.

lines.en: I would like to rent a bike.
Twenty. Bring it back before six.

title: At the bank
aim: Ask to open an account, simply.

lines.en: I would like to open an account.
Please sit down. This will take a few minutes.

title: The cash machine
aim: Say the machine did not give the money.

lines.en: Did it give you the money?
Call the number on the screen. Do not leave the card.

title: A job advert
aim: Ask about a simple job.

title: The first day
aim: Ask where things are on your first day.

lines.en: Where do I get a password?
Ask your colleague. She will show you.

title: A meeting time
aim: Move a meeting politely.

title: An email
aim: Say you sent a file.

lines.en: I have not received it yet.

title: The classroom rules
aim: Ask if you may leave early.

lines.en: Yes. Please tell the class next time.

title: Asking a classmate
aim: Ask to borrow notes.

lines.en: Yes. I will share them tonight.

title: The sports club
aim: Ask about joining a class.

lines.en: Yes. The class is on Wednesday.
How much is it a week?
Ten. The first class is free.

title: The cinema
aim: Suggest a film and a time.

lines.en: Better. I will buy the tickets.

title: A birthday
aim: Invite someone to a small party.

lines.en: It is my birthday on Saturday.

title: The weather and plans
aim: Change a plan because of rain.

lines.en: It is raining. Shall we cancel?

title: Describing a person
aim: Describe someone so a friend can find them.

lines.en: She is tall and wears glasses.
Dark. She is wearing a blue coat.

title: Comparing two flats
aim: Say which place you prefer and why.

lines.en: The other one is closer to work.
Then this one is better for you.

title: A polite complaint
aim: Say something is wrong without being rude.

lines.en: I am sorry, but this is damaged.
Thank you. I do not need the manager.

title: What I did last week
aim: Tell a short story in the past.

lines.en: What did you do last week?
I visited my parents because my father was ill.
Three days. He is better now.

title: A plan for tomorrow
aim: Say what you are going to do.

lines.en: Tomorrow I am going to finish the report.
Then I will call the client.
Do you need help with the figures?

title: Changing a plan
aim: Explain why you have to change a plan.

lines.en: Unfortunately I have to change our plan.
The meeting was moved, so I cannot come at one.
We can still meet at four.

title: At the office
aim: Explain what you are working on.

lines.en: The client project. I am responsible for the text.
Friday. I will send an update tonight.

title: Asking a colleague
aim: Ask for help without stopping someone's work.

lines.en: Could you show me how this form works?
Yes. If it takes longer, we can continue later.

title: A deadline
aim: Say you may miss a deadline and propose a new time.

lines.en: The figures arrived late. I propose Monday.
Monday is enough if the rest is ready.

title: Working from home
aim: Agree which days you will be in the office.

lines.en: I will work from home on Thursday.
Yes. Call me if something is urgent.
I will be in the office.

title: A short interview
aim: Answer why you want the job.

lines.en: Why do you want this job?
Because I want to learn, and I like working in a team.
I worked in a shop for two years, so I am used to customers.

title: Giving a reason
aim: Explain a decision with because.

lines.en: We decided to take the train.
Because it saves time, even though it costs more.
That makes sense if the meeting is at six.

title: In a meeting
aim: Ask someone to repeat a point.

lines.en: I mean we should start the report this week.
I agree, and I will take notes.
Good. Send them to the team.

title: A presentation
aim: Introduce what you are going to talk about.

lines.en: Today I am going to talk about the market.
Ten minutes. First the problem, then the idea, and finally a question.

title: I disagree
aim: Disagree politely in class.

lines.en: I disagree, however I see your point.
In my opinion the smaller shop is better for students.

title: Group work problem
aim: Say someone has not done their part.

lines.en: Lea has not sent her part yet.
It is not fair if we do her work.
Let us talk to her before we tell the teacher.

title: Asking for an extension
aim: Ask a teacher for more time.

lines.en: Because I was ill last week. I can send a draft on Monday.

title: The exam
aim: Ask what the exam will cover.

lines.en: No. Revise the examples from class.

title: At the clinic
aim: Describe symptoms over several days.

lines.en: A cough for three days, and it is worse at night.

title: Medicine instructions
aim: Check how to take medicine.

lines.en: Do I take it with food?
No. Call us if you notice a side effect.

title: Booking online
aim: Say the website would not take your payment.

lines.en: The payment failed on the website.
Did the money leave your account?
Try again in an hour, or pay here.

title: A missed connection
aim: Explain you missed a train and ask for the next one.

lines.en: The next train is at four.
Yes. You do not need a new ticket.

title: At the airport
aim: Ask which desk and what to show.

lines.en: Desk twelve. Have your passport ready.
Not yet. Boarding starts at six.

title: The luggage
aim: Report a bag that did not arrive.

lines.en: A blue suitcase with a red label.
Please fill in this form. We will call you.

title: Renting a flat
aim: Ask about rent, bills, and the contract.

lines.en: Water is included. Electricity is not.

title: A noisy flat
aim: Explain a housing problem to the agency.

lines.en: The people upstairs are noisy at night.
I will ask them to keep it down.

title: The repair
aim: Arrange a time for a repair.

lines.en: The repair person can come on Tuesday.
I am not available in the morning.
Yes. I will be there to let them in.

title: At the bank again
aim: Question a charge you do not recognise.

lines.en: I do not recognise this charge.
I was not in that shop.
We can block the card while we check.

title: A budget
aim: Talk about spending too much.

lines.en: Did you keep to the budget?
No. I spent too much on the train.
Is there enough for the hotel?
Yes, if we save on meals.

title: Inviting formally
aim: Invite someone and give them a way to refuse.

lines.en: I would like to invite you to dinner.
Yes, if you can. If not, another time is fine.

title: Apologising
aim: Apologise and say how you will fix it.

lines.en: I am sorry. It was my fault.
I forgot the file. I will send it today.
Thank you. Please check it first.

title: Giving advice
aim: Advise a friend who is tired.

title: A complaint at work
aim: Say a process is wasting time.

lines.en: Write it down and we will discuss it.

title: Customer on the phone
aim: Calm a customer and promise a time.

lines.en: I will look into the problem.
That we will call by four.

title: The school trip
aim: Ask about cost and permission.

lines.en: Do we need permission for the trip?
Yes, from a parent if you are under eighteen.

title: Volunteering
aim: Offer to help and ask what is needed.

lines.en: We need help on Saturday morning.

title: A neighbourhood meeting
aim: Give an opinion about a local plan.

lines.en: If it closes at nine, that should be fine.
I will mention that at the meeting.

title: Recycling
aim: Ask which bin to use.

lines.en: The yellow one. Paper is blue.

title: The dentist
aim: Cancel and rebook an appointment.

lines.en: I need to cancel my appointment.

title: At the gym
aim: Ask a beginner question.

title: Food for a guest
aim: Ask about food a guest cannot eat.

title: A review
aim: Explain why you would or would not return.

lines.en: The food was good, but the service was slow.
Yes, if we have more time.

title: Comparing prices
aim: Explain why the cheaper one is not better.

lines.en: The quality is not the same.
Is the expensive one worth it?
If you will use it every day, yes.

title: Online shopping
aim: Ask about delivery and returns.

title: A misunderstanding
aim: Correct what you thought someone meant.

title: Saying no politely
aim: Refuse extra work and give a reason.

lines.en: Can you take this as well?
I cannot. I already have the report.
Yes. Next week I have time.

title: The news
aim: Give a short reaction to a local story.

lines.en: Yes. The repairs start in May.
I hope it does not affect the morning train.

title: A recommendation
aim: Recommend a place and say why.

lines.en: The one by the park. It is quiet.
Yes. Avoid the one at the station. It is loud.

title: Travel insurance
aim: Ask what a policy covers.

lines.en: Does it cover a missed flight?

title: A parents' evening
aim: Report how a student is doing.

lines.en: More than before. Her writing is careful.

title: Team roles
aim: Clarify who does what.

lines.en: Who is in charge of the budget?
I am. You support the client.

title: After the mistake
aim: Describe a mistake and what you learned.

lines.en: I noticed a mistake in the numbers.
No. I checked again and sent a correction.
Next time, ask someone to read it too.

title: Choosing a course
aim: Compare two courses.

lines.en: The other one has more theory.
If you want a job soon, take the practical one.

title: Opening a meeting
aim: Start a meeting and set the purpose.

lines.en: The purpose of this meeting is to agree the timeline.
Yes. The outcome we need is a date, and we have thirty minutes.
Then let us start with the risks.

title: Interrupting politely
aim: Come in on a point without cutting someone off.

lines.en: May I add something before we move on?
Please, if it is on this point.
Go ahead, then I will finish.

title: Summarising
aim: Summarise what was agreed.

lines.en: We agreed to send the draft on Monday.
The action is mine, and you will review it.
Yes. I will send comments by Wednesday.

title: Disagreeing with a manager
aim: Disagree while staying respectful.

lines.en: The date is possible. However, the risk is quality.

title: Giving feedback
aim: Give feedback that is specific and kind.

lines.en: Your strength is the clear structure.
Thank you. What should I improve?
The examples. In section two, one case would help.

title: Receiving feedback
aim: Respond to criticism without defending every point.

lines.en: I was not sure you would see it that way.
I partly disagree about the tone, but I will try a shorter ending.

title: Negotiating a deadline
aim: Trade scope for time.

lines.en: Monday is not realistic if the scope stays the same.
The appendix. If we drop it, Monday is possible.

title: A salary conversation
aim: Ask for a review with reasons.

lines.en: I would like to discuss my salary.
I have taken on more responsibility, and the market rate is higher.
Bring a short note, and we will review it next month.

title: Working across teams
aim: Explain a delay caused by another team.

lines.en: We are blocked because we depend on their data.
Yes. Meanwhile we can draft the rest.
Do that, and copy me on the next email.

title: A difficult client
aim: Set a boundary with a client.

lines.en: The client wants another round of changes.
We can do it, but we should charge for the extra work.

title: In a seminar
aim: Build on someone else's idea.

lines.en: I would like to build on what you said.
The claim is interesting, whereas the evidence is still thin.

title: Citing a source
aim: Say where an idea comes from.

lines.en: According to the article, prices fell.
They argue it clearly. However, the sample is small.

title: A tutorial
aim: Ask for clarification of a theory.

lines.en: In other words, the theory says demand falls when the price rises.
How does that apply to this case?
The ticket price rose, and fewer people travelled.

title: Peer review
aim: Comment on a classmate's draft.

lines.en: The third paragraph repeats the second.
I suggest you end with the question, not the definition.

title: An academic disagreement
aim: Hold a disagreement without making it personal.

lines.en: My position is not that the plan is wrong.
Rather, that the evidence does not yet support it.
Then we disagree about the evidence, not about the aim.

title: Office hours
aim: Prepare a useful question for a teacher.

lines.en: I am stuck on question four.
The method from class. The last step fails.
Bring the page to office hours. A specific question is easier to answer.

title: Choosing a research topic
aim: Narrow a topic that is too wide.

lines.en: I could focus on one city.
Yes. That is a topic I can finish.

title: A presentation question
aim: Answer a question you only partly know.

lines.en: What happens if the cost doubles?
I am not sure of the exact figure.
Partly, demand would fall. I will check and follow up.

title: Ethics
aim: Raise an ethical problem in a study.

lines.en: Yes, and the data is anonymous.
We should still say how long we keep it.

title: After the results
aim: Explain a result that was not what you expected.

lines.en: However, the groups were almost the same.
Then the next step is to ask why, not to hide the result.

title: The contract
aim: Ask what a clause means before you sign.

lines.en: Either side can end the contract with one month's notice.
Only if you damage it. Read it before you sign.

title: Remote work limits
aim: Negotiate which hours you will be online.

lines.en: I can overlap with the team from ten to three.
We expect people online in those core hours.
Outside that, I will answer the next morning.
That is reasonable if the work is not urgent.

title: A performance review
aim: Talk about the year without only listing tasks.

lines.en: I shortened the client process, and I learned to run the weekly meeting.
I would like to lead a small project.

title: Pushing back on scope
aim: Protect the team from extra work.

lines.en: If we add this, something else has to wait.
Then we choose. Speed or quality. That is the trade-off.

title: Writing it down
aim: Insist on a written decision.

lines.en: Can we confirm this in writing?
We said it in the meeting.
Yes, and people assume different things later.
I will send a short note, to avoid that.

title: The news article
aim: Question a headline.

lines.en: The headline says the school will close.
The article only says they are discussing it.
So the claim is stronger than the source.
I am sceptical until we see the decision.

title: A public meeting
aim: Make a point and yield the floor.

lines.en: My concern is the night buses, not the park itself.
Thank you. I will hand over to the next person.

title: Housing choice
aim: Weigh two homes with although and because.

lines.en: Although the other flat is closer, I would choose this one.
Yes. The quiet is worth the longer walk.
On balance, I might choose differently.

title: A family decision
aim: Disagree with family and still decide together.

lines.en: I would rather stay in the city.
It depends on what matters to you. School matters to me.
Then we should look at both.
Yes. We decide together, not tonight.

title: Care for a parent
aim: Talk about help for a parent without deciding for them.

lines.en: She prefers to stay at home.
With support, yes. Rather than move her, we could visit every day.
Ask her before we arrange anything.

title: A second opinion
aim: Ask for another medical opinion politely.

lines.en: I would like a second opinion.
Of course. It does not mean you doubt the first doctor.
I want to be sure of the options.
I will write a referral. You can change your mind.

title: Insurance small print
aim: Question what is not covered.

lines.en: Yes, unless it is an emergency.
I need to check that before I travel.
The full list is on the second page.

title: At the embassy
aim: Explain why you need an appointment urgently.

lines.en: I need an earlier appointment because I travel on the twelfth.
Bring the documents and we will see what is possible.
Is a letter from my employer useful?
Yes. It shows why the date matters.

title: Culture and time
aim: Talk about different habits without judging.

lines.en: At home we tend to arrive a little late.
Whereas here, meetings start on time.
I am used to that now.
Neither habit is wrong. It helps to know which one you are in.

title: A complaint letter
aim: Structure a written complaint.

lines.en: State what you bought, what went wrong, and what you expect.
I expect a replacement or a refund.
Attach the receipt, and give them a date to resolve it.

title: Negotiating a price
aim: Ask for a better price with a reason.

lines.en: If I take three, is there a discount?
I can take ten percent off.
Can you meet me at fifteen?

title: The environment at work
aim: Propose a change and admit the cost.

lines.en: I propose we stop printing the weekly pack.
Yes. It wastes paper. We could trial a month without it.
A trial is easier to accept than a permanent rule.

title: Mentoring
aim: Ask a mentor for advice, not for them to do the job.

lines.en: I would like your advice rather than a solution.
Tell me what you have already decided.
I will keep the meeting short. I am less sure about the tone of the email.

title: After a conflict
aim: Repair a working relationship.

lines.en: We both assumed the other person would send the file.
I do not want to go over it again.
Nor do I. Let us agree how we work from here.

title: A careful recommendation
aim: Recommend someone without overselling.

lines.en: Yes, for research. That is her strength.
However, she is still learning to lead a meeting, so a small team would suit her better.

title: Reading a contract of sale
aim: Notice a condition before you buy.

lines.en: The warranty is void unless I register the product.
Register it today, or the promise is weaker.

title: Choosing not to decide
aim: Leave a decision open on purpose.

lines.en: I am not ready to decide yet.
Then I will decide when I have the second quote, not before.
That is reasonable. Do not rush the rest.

title: Two good options
aim: Show that both choices have a cost.

lines.en: Either we hire now, or we delay the launch.
If we hire, we spend money. If we delay, we lose the date.
Then we accept one cost openly.

title: What I would do
aim: Give advice using would, and mark it as yours.

lines.en: In your place, I would take the quieter flat.
Yes. However, that is my preference, not a rule for you.

title: Looking back
aim: Describe a change in your own view.

lines.en: I used to think the fastest option was always better.
Whereas now I think the calmer option lasts longer.

title: A reference
aim: Agree what a reference will and will not say.

lines.en: Yes. I will keep it accurate.
I will mention that strength, and I will not hide the fact that you have not led a team yet.

title: The exit interview
aim: Explain why you are leaving without attacking people.

lines.en: Mainly because of the opportunity, not because of the team.
Clearer priorities. I am grateful for the rest.

title: Chairing fairly
aim: Make sure a quiet person is heard.

lines.en: We have not heard from you yet.
I agree with the date, with one condition.
Please give your view before we close.
The budget has to be checked first.

title: When evidence is weak
aim: Say the data is not enough.

lines.en: The evidence is insufficient to conclude that.
It suggests a pattern. It does not prove a cause.
Then we ask for further data.

title: Tone in writing
aim: Soften a sentence that sounds harsh.

lines.en: The content is right. The tone is not.
Same point: 'Could we look at this again?' rather than 'This is wrong.'
